title: Circumcision
lead: The removal of the foreskin, given to Abraham as the sign of God's covenant (Genesis 17:10–14) and kept by Jews on the eighth day to this day. The prophets called for circumcision of the heart (Deuteronomy 10:16; Jeremiah 4:4), and the early church decided Gentile believers need not be circumcised (Acts 15; Galatians 5:6).

sections.b: God gives circumcision to Abraham as the sign of the covenant, for every male on the eighth day, including slaves and foreigners in the household (Genesis 17:9–14). Moses' son is circumcised in a strange night scene on the way to Egypt (Exodus 4:24–26), and the generation born in the wilderness is circumcised at Gilgal before entering the land (Joshua 5:2–9). The law repeats the eighth-day rule (Leviticus 12:3), and the prophets call for a circumcised heart (Deuteronomy 10:16; 30:6; Jeremiah 4:4). Jesus was circumcised on the eighth day (Luke 2:21). The early church decided that Gentile believers need not be circumcised (Acts 15:1–29), and Paul writes that true circumcision is "of the heart, by the Spirit" (Romans 2:28–29) and that believers were circumcised "with a circumcision made without hands" in Christ (Colossians 2:11).
